newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares closer firmer in technical rebound.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares closer firmer in technical rebound.

text.p: 1605 GMT - Italian shares end higher largely in a technical rebound after heavy selling in recent days helped by the firmer trend from domestic bonds and the lira, while the market was generally thin ahead of key inflation figures, dealers said.

* Trading volumes were subdued ahead of Italian preliminary February CPI inflation figures from six Italian ciites at around 1630 GMT. Analysts expect a fall in CPI inflation to 2.5 percent year-on-year in February from an official figure of 2.6 percent in January. A further Italian five cities report on Friday.
* The blue chip Mib30 index ended up 1.69 percent at 18,439 and all-share Mibtel index closed 1.62 percent firmer at 12,357.

* Dealers said that investors continue to be uncertain with doubts remaining over Italy's prospects for entering a single European currency, but the government's determination to go forward with a mini-budget this year had helped sentiment.
* Financial holding group Compart gained throughout the day to close up 7.11 percent higher at 880 lire on the view that it might return to the Mib30 when the index is revised in March.

* Among the main blue chips, Olivetti shares were up 2.7 percent at 650 lire, Fiat 1.8 percent firmer at 5,190 lire, Pirelli 1.67 percent higher at 3,465 lire while Montedison ended up 1.96 percent at 1,250 lire.
* Banking group BCI rose 3.99 percent to 3,750 lire after news it was in accord to buy majority stake of Venezuelan Banco del Orinoco, reinforcing its presence in south America.
* However, Parmalat had a return of nerves as slipped 2.8 percent to 2,255 lire. Earlier this month, talk of a bond issue to finance an acquisition pushed the shares lower.
